newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prosecutors want 9 years for Serb war defendant.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors want 9 years for Serb war defendant.

text.p: German prosecutors on Tuesday demanded a nine-year jail sentence for a 34-year-old Bosnian Serb accused of taking part in the killing of almost 30 Moslems in 1992 during the Bosnian civil war.
The hearing is the first war crimes trial in Germany since the Nuremberg tribunal on Nazi war crimes more than 50 years ago.

State prosecutor Walter Hemberger said Novislav Djajic, charged with being an accomplice to murder and genocide, did not just tag along with Serb fighters during the Bosnian civil war but was strongly committed to the "Serb goal of genocide".

In his final statement, Hemberger said Djajic took part in the capture of 15 Moslems in the town of Trnovace on June 22, 1992, and knew they were to be taken away and shot. Other Moslems were shot during a raid on another town.
Djajic says he did not know that the Trnovace Moslems were going to be shot. During the other raid, he says he did not fire any shots and that his gun was broken.
Much of the evidence against Djajic comes from a Moslem from Trnovce who fled from his captors and appears to have been the only one of the 15 to have escaped death.

Djajic entered Germany in 1993 and was arrested in January 1996. He went on trial in Munich earlier this year after the international tribunal on former Yugoslavia in The Hague delegated the case back to Germany.

Although the alleged offences were not committed in Germany, Djajic is being tried there under a passage of international law which says the perpetrators of genocide should not receive shelter anywhere and can be tried abroad.
A verdict is expected within the next few days.
Another Bosnian Serb, Nikola Jorgic, is on trial in Duesseldorf accused of leading a death squad which massacred at least 22 Moslems in 1992 during the Serb campaign of "ethnic cleansing".
